Autumn Grand Festival (November 8) | Main Building = Single bay, {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|qid=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri|1=Shinmei-zukuri}} | Map = {{location map|Japan Tokyo|label=Musashi Mitake Shrine|float=center|relief=1|width=200|caption=}} }} '''Musashi Mitake Shrine''' (武蔵御嶽神社, Musashi Mitake Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located on {{ill|Mount Mitake (Tokyo)|en|Mount Mitake (Tokyo)|qid=Q1432565|lt=Mount Mitake (Tokyo)|1=Mount Mitake (Tokyo)}} in {{ill|Ōme, Tokyo|en|Ōme, Tokyo|qid=Q237683|lt=Ōme, Tokyo|1=Ōme, Tokyo}}, {{ill|Tokyo|en|Tokyo|qid=Q1490|lt=Tokyo|1=Tokyo}}, Japan, formerly part of {{ill|Musashi Province|en|Musashi Province|qid=Q907398|lt=Musashi Province|1=Musashi Province}}. The name "Mitake" or "Ontake" refers to the holy mountain {{ill|Kinpusen|ja|金峯山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinpusen|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 金峰山|1=Mount Kinpusen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10563986}}, central to the Shugendō tradition in {{ill|Yoshino, Nara|ja|吉野|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshino, Nara|1=Yoshino|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q15410122}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|qid=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}}. Enshrined deities include {{ill|Zaō Gongen|lt=Zaō Gongen|lt=Zao Gongen|ja|蔵王権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zao Gongen|qq=}} and {{ill|Kushimachi-no-Mikoto|ja|櫛真智命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushimachi-no-Mikoto|1=Kushimachi no Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q108039939}}, reflecting the shrine's role as a mountain {{ill|Haisho|ja|拝所|lt=worship site|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haisho|qq=}}. Recognized as a spiritual hub since the {{ill|Middle Ages|en|Middle Ages|qid=Q12554|lt=Middle Ages|1=Middle Ages}}, the shrine has developed a religious sphere encompassing the Musashi and Sagami provinces. It is theorized to correspond to the {{ill|Ōmazuto no Mitama Shrine|ja|大麻止乃豆天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmazuto no Mitama Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|qid=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki|1=Engishiki}}. Currently, it operates as an independent {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|単立神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 単立|redirects to 単立|1=Independent Shinto shrine|2=ja|3=単立|1=Independent Shinto shrine|2=ja|3=単立|redirects to 単立|1=Independent Shinto shrine|2=ja|3=単立|}} unaffiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|qid=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. The shrine also enshrines {{ill|Ōguchi no Magami|ja|大口真神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōguchi no Magami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 真神|1=Ōkuchi no Magami|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2349235}} ("Great Mouth True God"), known as the {{ill|Wolf deity|ja|狼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wolf deity|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオカミ|1=Wolf|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q18498}}, attracting visitors who bring their dogs as part of their prayers. Notably, the {{ill|Mitake Tozan Railway|en|Mitake Tozan Railway|qid=Q6880754|lt=Mitake Tozan Railway|1=Mitake Tozan Railway}} allows dogs to board without a cage. == Deities == * {{ill|Zaō Gongen|lt=Zaō Gongen|lt=Zao Gongen|ja|蔵王権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zao Gongen|qq=}} * {{ill|Kushimachi-no-Mikoto|ja|櫛真智命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushimachi-no-Mikoto|1=Kushimachi no Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q108039939}} * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}} * {{ill|Sukunahikona|ja|少彦名命|1=Sukunabikona|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunahikona|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スクナビコナ}} * {{ill|Emperor Ankan|en|Emperor Ankan|qid=Q241765|lt=Emperor Ankan|1=Emperor Ankan}} * {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q461258}} == History == The shrine is traditionally said to have been established during the 7th year of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin|1=Emperor Sujin}}'s reign (91 BCE). {{ill|Gyōki|en|Gyōki|qid=Q1136664|lt=Gyōki|1=Gyōki}} is believed to have enshrined {{ill|Zaō Gongen|lt=Zaō Gongen|lt=Zao Gongen|ja|蔵王権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zao Gongen|qq=}} here in the 8th year of the Tenpyō era (736 CE). In the first year of Bunryaku (1234), {{ill|Ōnakatomi Kunikane|ja|大中臣国兼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōnakatomi Kunikane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} restored the shrine's buildings, which had fallen into disrepair. The shrine became known as a training ground for {{ill|Shugendō|en|Shugendō|qid=Q1483875|lt=Shugendō|1=Shugendō}}, receiving numerous offerings from samurai families. During the Edo period, the shrine underwent major renovations, including a reconstruction of the main hall in 1605 under {{ill|Ōkubo Nagayasu|en|Ōkubo Nagayasu|qid=Q133746|lt=Ōkubo Nagayasu|1=Ōkubo Nagayasu}}. With the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|en|Shinbutsu bunri|qid=Q1970535|lt=Shinbutsu bunri|1=Shinbutsu bunri}} policy in the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed "Ōmazuto no Mitama Shrine," theorized as the shrine mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|qid=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki|1=Engishiki}}. This name was later changed to "Mitake Shrine" due to other shrines making similar claims. In 1952, it was renamed "Musashi Mitake Shrine." == Facilities and Structures == {{ill|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image:武蔵御岳神社_本殿.jpg|thumb|200px|Main Hall|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|qq=}} The main hall ({{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|en|Haiden (Shinto)|qid=Q3125745|lt=Haiden|1=Haiden (Shinto)}}) is an elaborate structure with red paint, carvings, and a {{ill|Karahafu|en|Karahafu|qid=Q977293|lt=Karahafu|1=Karahafu}} gable. The current main sanctuary ({{ill|Honden|en|Honden|qid=Q2044994|lt=Honden|1=Honden}}) was rebuilt in 1877 in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|qid=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri|1=Shinmei-zukuri}} style. The shrine features numerous subsidiary shrines, including the {{ill|Ōguchi no Magami Shrine|ja|大口真神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōguchi no Magami Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a remote shrine for mountain worship (Okumiya), and a treasure hall housing national treasures such as the {{ill|Aka-ito Odoshi Yoroi|ja|赤糸威鎧|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aka-ito Odoshi Yoroi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} armor. == Festivals == Major festivals include: * January 1: {{ill|New Year Festival|ja|元旦祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/New Year Festival|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to
